# Discovery-to-deployment contract, version 3.0

Repair the provided multi-file project. `submission/run.py` is the single-request
entry point; its source modules are part of the submission. The deployed result
is a deterministic certificate and replay, not a trained neural classifier.
Packet capture, neural training and activation generation are outside this CPU
profile: prepared packet features and activation maps are supplied explicitly.

## Input and arithmetic

Read one UTF-8 JSON object to EOF, <=64MiB, container nesting<=32 (root depth1).
Malformed JSON and invalid UTF-8 are invalid. Integer fields require JSON integer
tokens without a decimal point or exponent: `3.0` and `3e0` are invalid.
Duplicate keys, nonfinite constants, extra keys, trailing data, invalid shapes,
non-integers where integers are specified, booleans as integers, and violations
of any bound or lifecycle rule require exactly `{"error":"invalid_request"}` and
exit0, without partial certificates. Valid requests also exit0 and return one
JSON object. JSON object order/whitespace do not matter; array order and types do.
All fractions below are pairs `[p,q]`, integers 0<=p<=1000000,1<=q<=1000000;
nonreduced input is allowed. Output fractions must be reduced with positive q.
All stated inequalities and square roots are mathematical, without tolerances.
IDs match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}`; string order is ASCII order.

Root keys are exactly `capacity`, `releases`, `blocks`.
`capacity` has exactly `range` (integer0..4096) and `exact` (integer0..8192).
These are separate entry pools for resident range and exact-match release banks.
`releases` is an array1..8 with unique IDs; `blocks` is an array0..20000 of arrays
of operations. Empty blocks are allowed. Flattening blocks defines zero-based
operation indices `at`; block boundaries have no other effect.

A release has exactly: `id`, `classes` (integer1..16), `width` (integer2..16),
`eps`, `ratio`, `threshold` (fractions, with ratio<=1), `mode` (`range` or `exact`),
`packet_limit` (integer width..200000), `idle_us` (integer0..1000000000000),
`discovery`, `train`, `validation` (arrays of rows).
Every row has exactly `class` (integer0..classes-1), `values` (integer array).
Discovery rows additionally have `activation` (integer array, same length as
values, entries0..1000000). Discovery values have length2..128; other rows0..128.
Every train and validation array contains at least one row from every class.
A discovery array may be empty or omit classes.

Values use the project's encoding: signed packet length +1514, in0..3028.
1514 is padding, never a real packet. Padding is allowed only as a suffix.
The real prefix stops before its first1514. Empty and all-padding flows are legal.
All coordinates, including padded coordinates, count toward input budgets.
Across the WHOLE request: discovery<=4096rows, train<=8192rows,
validation<=8192rows, total values across these three arrays<=1048576,
derived fragments<=4096, packets<=200000, opens<=8192, installs<=2048,
and operations<=218432. Counts span every release and block.

## Discovery certificate

For each discovery row, define mean and population standard deviation of its
activation values over the REAL prefix only. A position is high iff its value
is strictly greater than mean+standard-deviation. Maximal consecutive high runs
are separated by any non-high position or the end of the real prefix. Discard
runs shorter than2. A run of length2..width contributes that entire fragment.
A longer run contributes its width-long window with greatest activation sum;
equal sums select the earliest start, including the final legal window.

Fragment IDs are zero-based discovery order: source-row order, then run order.
A fragment certificate is `[source_row_index,start_position,length]`; positions
are zero-based within the original row. Its feature sequence is the corresponding
real values. Multiplicity is preserved even for identical sequences.

Clustering is separate for each class and fragment length. Let m be the total
fragment count in that class ACROSS lengths; density minimum is max(2,ceil(m*ratio)).
For equal-length sequences a,b of length L, let A be the number of equal
coordinates. Each coordinate distance is abs(a-b), plus1000 exactly when one
value is strictly below1514 and the other strictly above1514. Their distance is
sqrt(sum(coordinate_distance^2)/L)*(3/5)^A. Neighbors have distance<=eps,
including a sequence itself and duplicate sequences as separate fragments.

A core fragment has at least the density minimum neighbors of its own class
and length. Each connected component of the neighbor graph on CORE fragments
is one cluster. A noncore fragment adjacent to cores belongs to the component
whose smallest core fragment ID is smallest. All remaining fragments are noise.
A cluster ID is its smallest core fragment ID. Membership includes attached
noncore fragments; `core` lists only core members. Both lists are sorted IDs.

For each coordinate of all members, let lo,hi be its min/max and sigma its
population standard deviation. The generalized interval is
[max(0,trunc(lo-sigma)),min(3028,trunc(hi+sigma))], where trunc is toward zero.
Clustering and these boundaries must be exact, including eps and sigma equality.

## Calibration and backup

A validation row matches a generalized interval pattern iff some contiguous
real-prefix window of the same length lies inside every inclusive interval.
A row contributes once per pattern, regardless of overlapping/repeated matches.
For a cluster, `hits[c]` is the matching validation-row count of class c, and N[c]
is that class's total validation-row count. For its target class t,
Cin=hits[t]/N[t]; Cout=max(hits[c]/N[c] for c!=t), or0 if no other class.
Its score is Cin/(Cout+1/10000). It is kept iff score>threshold. No forced backup
patterns are added when none survive. Priority is decreasing EXACT score,
then increasing cluster ID; it is shared across classes and lengths.

Train the backup using the provided CPU decision-tree path, with exactly
scikit-learn1.4.2 DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=10,random_state=42,
class_weight='balanced'), all other constructor defaults. Each training row is
its first width encoded values, right-padded with1514, labelled by class.
Training-row order is the input order. This pinned library behavior defines
this stage; no claim of globally optimal classifier training is made.
The backup certificate uses its native tree-node order. A leaf is `[class]`,
where class is the smallest model.classes_ value with maximum leaf value.
A branch is `[feature_index,2*threshold,left_child_index,right_child_index]`.
Features are integers here, so twice the fitted midpoint threshold is integral.
All certificate entries are JSON integers. Prediction takes left iff
2*feature<=2*threshold; input truncation/padding is the same as training.

## Tables and release banks

A range bank needs one entry per kept cluster. An exact bank has separate tables
for each pattern length. Each pattern denotes its Cartesian product of integer
interval values, excluding1514 at EVERY coordinate. Identical exact keys of the
same length occupy one entry; their action is the highest-priority matching
cluster. Keys of different lengths are distinct. The exact certificate entry
count is min(actual distinct keys,capacity.exact+1). Only this clipped count is part of the
certificate. Range counts are not clipped.

Operations have exactly these shapes:

* `["install",release_id]`: attempt to make that release current atomically.
* `["open",flow_id]`: open an inactive flow using the CURRENT release, which must
  exist. Its epoch starts at0 and increments each time that flow ID is reopened.
* `["packet",flow_id,timestamp_us,src,length]`: active flow; timestamp integer
  0..1000000000000, src integer0/1, length integer1..1514.
* `["close",flow_id]`: close an active epoch and release its bank reference.

A resident bank is either current or pinned by at least one open epoch. Each ID
occupies one bank even when current and pinned or reinstalled. When installing,
the previous current bank can be evicted iff it has no open references. If the
new bank alone exceeds its mode's capacity, status is `oversize`. Otherwise,
if the prospective resident banks exceed either capacity, status is `busy`.
Either failure leaves current/residents unchanged. Otherwise status is `ok` and
the new bank becomes current. Reinstalling any supplied ID is allowed.
Closing the last flow pinned to a noncurrent bank evicts it immediately.
Classified-but-not-closed epochs STILL pin their bank. There is no automatic
opening, expiry or final close: all opens must close by the end.

## Online behavior

Each epoch retains the release pinned at open, despite later successful installs.
Its first packet fixes positive direction: encoded feature is1514+length for
that src,1514-length for the other. Packet positions start at0 per epoch.
Timestamps must be nondecreasing within an epoch, even AFTER classification;
there is no cross-flow or cross-epoch timestamp ordering requirement.

For an unclassified arriving packet, idle backup has precedence if at least width
packets were already consumed and the gap from the previous packet is STRICTLY
larger than idle_us: commit backup BEFORE consuming the new packet.
Otherwise consume it. A segment match concerns a contiguous suffix ending at
this packet, with enough REAL packets for its length. At the earliest packet
with any match, commit the highest-priority matching cluster immediately.
A future match cannot replace this decision. If this packet has no match and
the consumed count is STRICTLY greater than packet_limit, commit backup instead.

Backup always uses the FIRST width encoded features of the epoch, frozen once
available. At an unclassified close, right-pad a shorter prefix with1514 and
commit backup, including a completely empty flow. A gap before width packets
does not classify or reset the epoch. Idle is checked only on an arriving packet,
not on close or a timer. After commitment, packets bypass matching and backup,
but timestamp validation and the open bank reference remain until close.

## Output certificate

Return exactly `catalog`, `installs`, `decisions`, `final`.
`catalog` follows release input order. Each item has exactly:

* `id`, `fragments` (triples defined above), `noise` (sorted fragment IDs).
* `clusters`, ordered by cluster ID. Each has exactly `id`, `class`, `members`,
  `core`, `range` (ordered [lo,hi] pairs), `hits` (class-index order),
  `score` (reduced fraction), `kept` (JSON boolean).
* `priority`: kept cluster IDs in priority order; `backup`: tree nodes defined
  above; `entries`: this bank's entry count, clipped only for exact mode.

`installs` follows install operation order. Each item has exactly `at`, `id`,
`status` (`ok`,`busy`,`oversize`), `resident` (sorted release IDs AFTER the attempt),
`used` (object with exact `range`,`exact` integer pool usage after the attempt).
`decisions` follows commitment order, exactly one per opened epoch. Each item:
`flow`, `epoch`, `release`, `at`, `seen`, `class`, `reason`, `rule`, `start`.
`seen` counts packets consumed at commitment: idle excludes the arriving packet;
segment/limit include it; close uses all consumed packets. `reason` is `segment`,
`idle`, `limit` or `close`. `rule` is the selected integer cluster ID and `start`
is its zero-based start packet position for segment, otherwise both are null.
The segment interval is [start,seen). `at` is the committing packet/close index.
`final` has exactly `current` (release ID or null), `resident` (sorted IDs),
`used` (the same two pool counts) after all operations and closes.

## Runtime, submission and public check

Use Python3.11.14 and the pinned offline CPU packages in wheels/manifest.json.
NumPy1.26.4, SciPy1.12.0, scikit-learn1.4.2, joblib1.4.2, threadpoolctl3.5.0 and
PyYAML6.0.2 and the pinned native zlib runtime in native/ are provided; no install/network access is needed from the internet.
`python3 prepare_env.py` prepares the supplied wheels offline as a nonroot user.
`python3 check.py submission` does that automatically, then runs only small public
sanity fixtures in real bounded children. It is not the acceptance suite.
The supplied project is a partial batch implementation, not a complete simulator
for this contract. Repair/extend its modules and integration. No neural or capture
dependency is missing: those paths are outside this supplied CPU profile.

Submit the whole submission/ project with run.py at its root: <=64MiB and
<=4096 regular file/directory entries. Symlinks, hard links and special files are
rejected. Any regular source/config/data files may be included within the budget;
no requirement to retain a particular implementation layout. Generated .git,
__pycache__,.pytest_cache,.ruff_cache directories are ignored at every depth and
must not supply runtime dependencies. Other extra regular files are allowed.
The checker freezes project bytes before execution. Only the frozen project and
provided dependencies are needed; dependency location is SYNECDOCHE_SITE.

One WHOLE request gets120CPU seconds soft/121hard,180wall seconds,1GiB address
space,32FDs,64MiB per regular file,zero core dumps,stdout<=16MiB,stderr<=1MiB.
These are feasibility bounds for a two-minute offline recalibration/deployment
job plus its supplied replay, not a timing score. Limits include parsing,
clustering, calibration, certificates and replay; budgets do not reset by stage.
Process/thread count is limited to64 by UID, and fork/vfork/clone are denied;
clone3 returns ENOSYS, so candidate subprocesses/threads cannot be used.
BLAS/OpenMP/MKL thread counts are1. A 250ms pathname sample above1GiB logical or
allocated scratch or50000entries (including root) is an infrastructure emergency
brake, not an exact storage quota. No scratch output is part of the answer.

Linux x86_64 seccomp denies sockets/socketpair/connect; SysV shared memory,
semaphores/messages; kill/tkill/tgkill; ptrace/process_vm access; namespace,
mount/pivot_root/chroot,setsid/setpgid; identity/group changes; file-handle access;
BPF,keyrings,perf_event_open,userfaultfd,io_uring and pidfd_getfd. Wrong syscall
architecture/x32 kills the process. Privileges cannot be regained. exec is allowed
inside the scoring filesystem boundary. Normal OS stdin/stdout support text,

Scored execution requires a nonprivileged allowlisted filesystem with immutable

PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1,PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and the three thread-count variables=1. LD_LIBRARY_PATH points only to the

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Public sanity checks: frozen candidate bytes in a bounded OS child."""
import argparse
import os
import json
import pathlib
import signal
import sys
from prepare_env import ensure_environment
from public_runner import PublicRunner, CandidateFailure, InfrastructureError


def unique(pairs):
    d = {}
    for k, v in pairs:
        if k in d:
            raise ValueError('duplicate JSON key')
        d[k] = v
    return d


def strict_json(data):
    def bad(_):
        raise ValueError('nonfinite JSON')
    return json.loads(data.decode('utf-8'), object_pairs_hook=unique, parse_constant=bad, parse_float=bad)


def equivalent(a, b):
    return json.dumps(a, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False) == json.dumps(b, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False)


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('submission', type=pathlib.Path)
    p.add_argument('--state', type=pathlib.Path, default=None, help='optional public scratch parent')
    p.add_argument('--timeout', type=float, default=180, help='public per-request wall budget, at most 180 seconds')
    args = p.parse_args()
    interrupted = [False]
    def stop(signum, frame):
        if not interrupted[0]:
            interrupted[0] = True
            # Ignore repeated signals while finally/context cleanup runs.
            signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN)
            signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal.SIG_IGN)
            raise InfrastructureError('checker interrupted')
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)
    try:
        if not 0 < args.timeout <= 180:
            raise InfrastructureError('public timeout must be positive and at most 180 seconds')
        if os.geteuid()==0:
            raise InfrastructureError('public checker must run as a nonroot user')
        site = ensure_environment()
        fixtures = json.loads(pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('examples.json').read_text())
        reports = []
        with PublicRunner(args.submission, args.state,site=site) as sb:
            for case in fixtures:
                data = (case['raw'].encode() if 'raw' in case else json.dumps(case['request'], separators=(',', ':')).encode())
                result = sb.invoke(data, timeout=args.timeout, stdout_limit=16*1024*1024, stderr_limit=1024*1024)
                if result.returncode:
                    raise CandidateFailure('nonzero candidate exit in ' + case['name'])
                try:
                    answer = strict_json(result.stdout)
                except (ValueError, UnicodeError, RecursionError) as exc:
                    raise CandidateFailure('invalid/empty candidate JSON in ' + case['name']) from exc
                if not equivalent(answer, case['response']):
                    raise CandidateFailure('answer mismatch in ' + case['name'])
                reports.append({'case':case['name'], 'seconds':result.seconds})
        # Cleanup finished. Linearize publication with termination blocked:
        # pending signals mean interrupted; signals after the pending check
        # belong to a completed check and cannot publish a contradictory result.
        signals = {signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGINT}
        signal.pthread_sigmask(signal.SIG_BLOCK, signals)
        if interrupted[0] or signal.sigpending() & signals:
            raise InfrastructureError('checker interrupted before publication')
        print(json.dumps({'status':'public_checks_passed','cases':reports}))
        return 0
    except CandidateFailure as exc:
        print(json.dumps({'status':'candidate_failure','message':str(exc)}))
        return 1
    except (InfrastructureError, OSError) as exc:
        print(json.dumps({'status':'infrastructure_error','message':str(exc)}))
        return 2


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
"""Offline, standard-library-only preparation for the provided CPU packages."""
import fcntl
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import stat
import tempfile


def ensure_environment():
    if os.geteuid()==0:
        raise OSError('prepare/check must run as a nonroot user')
    base = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    import ctypes
    for filename,digest in json.loads((base/'native/manifest.json').read_text()).items():
        library = base/'native'/filename
        if hashlib.sha256(library.read_bytes()).hexdigest()!=digest:
            raise OSError('native dependency checksum mismatch')
        ctypes.CDLL(str(library),mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL)
    import zipfile
    manifest = base/'wheels/manifest.json'
    signature = hashlib.sha256(manifest.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    site = base/'site'
    with (base/'site.lock').open('a+b') as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock,fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        marker = site/'.prepared'
        if marker.is_file() and marker.read_text()==signature:
            return site
        stage = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='.prepare-',dir=base))
        try:
            for item in json.loads(manifest.read_text()):
                wheel = base/'wheels'/item['file']
                if hashlib.sha256(wheel.read_bytes()).hexdigest()!=item['sha256']:
                    raise OSError('offline wheel checksum mismatch')
                with zipfile.ZipFile(wheel) as archive:
                    for entry in archive.infolist():
                        name = Path(entry.filename)
                        if name.is_absolute() or '..' in name.parts or stat.S_ISLNK(entry.external_attr>>16):
                            raise OSError('unsafe offline wheel entry')
                    archive.extractall(stage)
            (stage/'.prepared').write_text(signature)
            if site.exists():
                shutil.rmtree(site)
            os.replace(stage,site)
        finally:
            if stage.exists():
                shutil.rmtree(stage)
    return site


if __name__=='__main__':
    print(ensure_environment())

import ctypes
import os
from pathlib import Path

        request = read_request(sys.stdin.buffer)
        response = execute(request)

        response = {'error':'invalid_request'}

"""Request syntax and aggregate resource-domain validation."""
import json
import re
ID = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}\Z")
MAX_BYTES = 64*1024**2


def require(condition):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError('invalid_request')


def integer(value, lo, hi):
    return type(value) is int and lo <= value <= hi


def identifier(value):
    return type(value) is str and ID.fullmatch(value) is not None


def keys(obj, fields):
    return type(obj) is dict and set(obj) == set(fields.split())


def fraction(value, max_num=1000000):
    return (type(value) is list and len(value)==2 and
            integer(value[0],0,max_num) and integer(value[1],1,1000000))


def unique(pairs):
    result = {}
    for key,value in pairs:
        require(key not in result)
        result[key] = value
    return result


def constant(_):
    raise ValueError('invalid_request')


def real_values(values):
    try:
        return values[:values.index(1514)]
    except ValueError:
        return values


def validate(root):
    stack = [(root,1)]
    while stack:
        node,depth = stack.pop()
        if type(node) in (dict,list):
            require(depth<=32)
            stack.extend((x,depth+1) for x in (node.values() if type(node) is dict else node))
    require(keys(root,'capacity releases blocks'))
    require(keys(root['capacity'],'range exact'))
    require(integer(root['capacity']['range'],0,4096))
    require(integer(root['capacity']['exact'],0,8192))
    require(type(root['releases']) is list and 1<=len(root['releases'])<=8)
    require(type(root['blocks']) is list and len(root['blocks'])<=20000)
    totals = {'discovery':0,'train':0,'validation':0,'values':0,'packet':0,'open':0,'install':0,'ops':0}
    models = {}
    for model in root['releases']:
        require(keys(model,'id classes width eps ratio threshold mode packet_limit idle_us discovery train validation'))
        require(identifier(model['id']) and model['id'] not in models)
        require(integer(model['classes'],1,16) and integer(model['width'],2,16))
        require(fraction(model['eps']) and fraction(model['ratio']))
        require(model['ratio'][0]<=model['ratio'][1])
        require(fraction(model['threshold']))
        require(type(model['mode']) is str and model['mode'] in ('range','exact'))
        require(integer(model['packet_limit'],model['width'],200000))
        require(integer(model['idle_us'],0,10**12))
        for group in ('discovery','train','validation'):
            rows = model[group]
            require(type(rows) is list)
            labels = set()
            totals[group] += len(rows)
            for row in rows:
                require(keys(row,'class values activation' if group=='discovery' else 'class values'))
                require(integer(row['class'],0,model['classes']-1))
                labels.add(row['class'])
                v = row['values']
                require(type(v) is list and (2 if group=='discovery' else 0)<=len(v)<=128)
                padding = False
                for value in v:
                    require(integer(value,0,3028))
                    padding = padding or value==1514
                    require(not padding or value==1514)
                totals['values'] += len(v)
                if group=='discovery':
                    scores = row['activation']
                    require(type(scores) is list and len(scores)==len(v))
                    require(all(integer(x,0,1000000) for x in scores))
            if group!='discovery':
                require(labels==set(range(model['classes'])))
        models[model['id']] = model
    require(totals['discovery']<=4096 and totals['train']<=8192 and totals['validation']<=8192)
    require(totals['values']<=1048576)
    for block in root['blocks']:
        require(type(block) is list)
        for event in block:
            require(type(event) is list and len(event)>=2 and type(event[0]) is str)
            op = event[0]
            require(op in ('install','open','packet','close') and identifier(event[1]))
            require(len(event)==(5 if op=='packet' else 2))
            totals['ops'] += 1
            if op in ('install','open','packet'):
                totals[op] += 1
            if op=='install':
                require(event[1] in models)
            if op=='packet':
                require(integer(event[2],0,10**12) and integer(event[3],0,1) and integer(event[4],1,1514))
    require(totals['ops']<=218432 and totals['packet']<=200000 and totals['open']<=8192 and totals['install']<=2048)
    return root


def bounded_containers(data):
    # The published row/operation/block maxima imply fewer than300000
    # containers in every valid request. Reject larger malformed structures
    # before allocating an unrestricted JSON object graph.
    depth = count = 0
    quoted = False
    last_slash = -2
    odd_slashes = False
    for token in re.finditer(rb'["\\\[\]{}]',data):
        at = token.start()
        char = data[at]
        if quoted:
            if char==92:
                odd_slashes = not odd_slashes if last_slash==at-1 else True
                last_slash = at
            elif char==34 and not (last_slash==at-1 and odd_slashes):
                quoted = False
        elif char==34:
            quoted = True
        elif char in (91,123):
            depth += 1
            count += 1
            require(depth<=32 and count<=300000)
        elif char in (93,125):
            depth -= 1
            require(depth>=0)


def read_request(stream):
    data = stream.read(MAX_BYTES+1)
    require(len(data)<=MAX_BYTES)
    bounded_containers(data)
    return validate(json.loads(data.decode('utf-8'), object_pairs_hook=unique, parse_constant=constant))

import sys, math, json
import numpy as np
from collections import defaultdict
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN
from sklearn.metrics import pairwise_distances

def recover(seq):
    """Convert sequence to integer list format"""
    res = seq.squeeze()
    res = np.asarray(res, dtype=int).tolist()
    return res

def custom_distance_euclidean_style_anchor(list1, list2):
    """
    Calculate custom Euclidean distance between two lists (with anchor point weighting)
    Matching values (anchor points) reduce the total distance
    """
    if len(list1) != len(list2):
        raise ValueError('Lists must have the same length')
    squared_distance = 0
    anchor_points = 0
    for (a, b) in zip(list1, list2):
        if a < 1514 < b or b < 1514 < a:
            squared_distance += (abs(a - b) + 1000) ** 2
        else:
            squared_distance += (a - b) ** 2
        if a == b:
            anchor_points += 1
    squared_distance /= len(list1)
    distance = np.sqrt(squared_distance)
    while anchor_points > 0:
        distance *= 0.6
        anchor_points -= 1
    return distance

def calculate_cluster_representations(cluster):
    """
    Calculate multiple representations of a cluster (including range and mean-std)

    Args:
        cluster: cluster data, list of lists, each inner list represents a sequence

    Returns:
        representations: dictionary containing two types of representations
            - 'range': [[min1, max1], [min2, max2], ...]
            - 'mean_std': [[mean1, std1], [mean2, std2], ...]
    """
    cluster_array = np.array(cluster)
    min_vals = np.min(cluster_array, axis=0)
    max_vals = np.max(cluster_array, axis=0)
    means = np.mean(cluster_array, axis=0)
    stds = np.std(cluster_array, axis=0)
    weights = 1 / (stds + 1) ** 2
    range_list = []
    for i in range(len(min_vals)):
        offset = 1 * stds[i]
        range_min = int(min_vals[i] - offset)
        range_max = int(max_vals[i] + offset)
        range_list.append([range_min, range_max])
    mean_list = []
    weights_list = []
    for i in range(len(means)):
        mean_val = float(means[i])
        weights_val = float(weights[i])
        mean_list.append(mean_val)
        weights_list.append(weights_val)
    mean_std_list = [mean_list, weights_list]
    return {'range': range_list, 'mean_std': mean_std_list}

def clustering(snippets, eps, ratio, class_name):
    """
    Cluster extracted snippets and calculate multiple representations of cluster centers

    Args:
        snippets: list of extracted snippets
        eps: eps parameter for DBSCAN
        ratio: ratio used to calculate min_samples
        class_name: class name

    Returns:
        center_list: list of cluster centers, each element is a dictionary containing two representations:
            {'range': [[min, max], ...], 'mean_std': [[mean, std], ...]}
    """
    sequences_by_length = defaultdict(list)
    for seq in snippets:
        sequences_by_length[len(seq)].append(seq)
    clusters = defaultdict(list)
    current_label = 0
    min_samples = max(2, math.ceil(len(snippets) * ratio))
    for (length, seqs) in sequences_by_length.items():
        if len(seqs) > 1:
            distance_matrix = pairwise_distances(seqs, metric=custom_distance_euclidean_style_anchor)
            clustering_result = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples, metric='precomputed').fit(distance_matrix)
            cluster_labels = clustering_result.labels_
            unique_labels = np.unique(cluster_labels)
            unique_labels = unique_labels[unique_labels != -1]
            for ul in unique_labels:
                seqs_in_cluster = [seqs[i] for (i, label) in enumerate(cluster_labels) if label == ul]
                clusters[current_label + ul].extend(seqs_in_cluster)
            current_label += len(unique_labels)
    cluster_list = list(clusters.values())
    center_list = []
    for c in cluster_list:
        representations = calculate_cluster_representations(c)
        center_list.append(representations)
    return center_list

def find_high_activation_snippets(input_seq, cam, max_length):
    """
    Find snippets with the highest activation values

    Args:
        input_seq: input sequence list
        cam: corresponding class activation map
        max_length: maximum snippet length

    Returns:
        snippets: set of high-activation snippets
    """
    snippets = []
    for i in range(len(input_seq)):
        sequence = recover(input_seq[i])
        activations = cam[i].squeeze()
        threshold = np.mean(activations) + 1.0 * np.std(activations)
        j = 0
        while j < len(activations):
            if activations[j] > threshold:
                snippet = []
                while j < len(activations) and activations[j] > threshold:
                    if sequence[j] != 1514:
                        snippet.append((activations[j], sequence[j]))
                    j += 1
                snippet_length = len(snippet)
                if 2 <= snippet_length <= max_length:
                    snippets.append(tuple((seq for (_, seq) in snippet)))
                elif snippet_length > max_length:
                    max_sum = float('-inf')
                    max_start = 0
                    for k in range(snippet_length - max_length):
                        current_sum = sum((snippet[x][0] for x in range(k, k + max_length)))
                        if current_sum > max_sum:
                            max_sum = current_sum
                            max_start = k
                    top_snippet = snippet[max_start:max_start + max_length]
                    snippets.append(tuple((seq for (_, seq) in top_snippet)))
            else:
                j += 1
    return snippets

import sys
import numpy as np

def euclidean_distance_between_ts(a, b, weight):
    """
    Calculate the minimum Euclidean distance between time series and shapelet.
    """
    a = np.array(a).squeeze()
    b = np.array(b).squeeze()
    min_distance = float('inf')
    len_a = len(a)
    len_b = len(b)
    match_point = 0
    if len_a == len_b:
        min_distance = np.linalg.norm(weight * (a - b))
    elif len_a < len_b:
        for start in range(len_b - len_a + 1):
            end = start + len_a
            distance = np.linalg.norm(weight * (b[start:end] - a)) / len_a
            if distance < min_distance:
                min_distance = distance
                match_point = end
    else:
        for start in range(len_a - len_b + 1):
            end = start + len_b
            distance = np.linalg.norm(weight * (a[start:end] - b)) / len_b
            if distance < min_distance:
                min_distance = distance
                match_point = end
    return (min_distance, match_point)

def check_range_shapelet_match(sample, range_shapelet):
    """
    Check if the sample sequence can match the range shapelet at some position.

    Args:
        sample: Sample sequence (1D array)
        range_shapelet: Range shapelet, format: [[min1, max1], [min2, max2], ...]

    Returns:
        bool: Whether matching is successful
    """
    sample_length = len(sample)
    shapelet_length = len(range_shapelet)
    if shapelet_length > sample_length:
        return False
    for start_pos in range(sample_length - shapelet_length + 1):
        match = True
        for (i, (range_min, range_max)) in enumerate(range_shapelet):
            sample_value = sample[start_pos + i]
            if not range_min <= sample_value <= range_max:
                match = False
                break
        if match:
            return True
    return False

def calculate_range_shapelet_coverage(range_shapelet, data_samples):
    """
    Calculate the coverage rate of range shapelet in given data samples.

    Args:
        range_shapelet: Range shapelet, format: [[min1, max1], [min2, max2], ...]
        data_samples: List of data samples

    Returns:
        float: Coverage rate (matched samples / total samples)
    """
    if len(data_samples) == 0:
        return 0.0
    matched_count = 0
    for sample in data_samples:
        if check_range_shapelet_match(sample, range_shapelet):
            matched_count += 1
    return matched_count / len(data_samples)

def _filter_shapelets_with_dual_representation(shapelets, train_seq_datagen, class_name, sample_num_target, sample_num_other, score):
    """
    Range shapelet filter: keep shapelets where intra-class coverage is greater than all other class coverage.
    Support shapelet dictionaries with multiple representation forms.

    Args:
        shapelets: List of shapelets, each element is a dictionary:
                  {'range': [[min1, max1], [min2, max2], ...],
                   'mean_std': [[mean1, std1], [mean2, std2], ...]}
        train_seq_datagen: Training data generator
        class_name: Target class name
        sample_num_target: Number of samples for target class
        sample_num_other: Number of samples for other classes
        score: Score threshold

    Returns:
        filtered_results: List of filtered results, each element is a (shapelet_dict, coverage_score) tuple
    """
    print(f'Starting filtering, original shapelet count: {len(shapelets)}', file=sys.stderr)
    all_class_names = train_seq_datagen.class_names
    other_class_names = [cls for cls in all_class_names if cls != class_name]
    print(f'Target class: {class_name}', file=sys.stderr)
    (target_data, *_) = train_seq_datagen.load_data_from_single_class(class_name, sample_num_target)
    print(f'Target class samples: {len(target_data)}', file=sys.stderr)
    if len(other_class_names) == 0:
        print('Warning: No other classes, return all shapelets (score as maximum value)', file=sys.stderr)
        return [(shapelet, 1000) for shapelet in shapelets]
    other_classes_data = {}
    max_class_num = max(train_seq_datagen.class_nums.values())
    ratio = sample_num_other / max_class_num
    for other_class in other_class_names:
        sample_num = int(train_seq_datagen.class_nums[other_class] * ratio)
        (other_data, *_) = train_seq_datagen.load_data_from_single_class(other_class, sample_num)
        other_classes_data[other_class] = other_data
    print(f'Other class samples loaded', file=sys.stderr)
    filtered_results = []
    rejected_count = 0
    all_shapelet_scores = []
    for (i, shapelet_dict) in enumerate(shapelets):
        range_shapelet = shapelet_dict['range']
        target_class_coverage = calculate_range_shapelet_coverage(range_shapelet, target_data)
        other_coverages = {}
        for (other_class, other_data) in other_classes_data.items():
            other_coverage = calculate_range_shapelet_coverage(range_shapelet, other_data)
            other_coverages[other_class] = other_coverage
        max_other_coverage = max(other_coverages.values()) if other_coverages else 0.0
        weight = [i.shape[0] for i in other_classes_data.values()]
        mean_other_coverage = np.average(list(other_coverages.values()), weights=weight) if other_coverages else 0.0
        all_shapelet_scores.append((i, max_other_coverage, shapelet_dict, target_class_coverage))
        score_1 = int(target_class_coverage / (mean_other_coverage + 0.0001))
        score_2 = target_class_coverage / (max_other_coverage + 0.0001)
        if score_2 > score:
            filtered_results.append((shapelet_dict, int(score_1)))
        else:
            rejected_count += 1
    reduction_ratio = rejected_count / len(shapelets) if len(shapelets) > 0 else 0
    print(f'\nFiltering completed:', file=sys.stderr)
    print(f'  Original count: {len(shapelets)}', file=sys.stderr)
    print(f'  Kept count: {len(filtered_results)}', file=sys.stderr)
    print(f'  Rejected count: {rejected_count}', file=sys.stderr)
    print(f'  Rejection ratio: {reduction_ratio:.1%}', file=sys.stderr)
    if len(filtered_results) == 0:
        print('Warning: All shapelets were filtered out, return the bottom 10% with lowest maximum coverage among other classes as backup', file=sys.stderr)
        all_shapelet_scores.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
        backup_count = max(1, len(shapelets) // 10)
        backup_results = []
        for item in all_shapelet_scores[:backup_count]:
            (_, max_other_coverage, shapelet_dict, _) = item
            score_val = int(1 / (max_other_coverage + 0.001))
            backup_results.append((shapelet_dict, score_val))
        print(f'  Return {len(backup_results)} shapelets with lowest maximum coverage among other classes as backup', file=sys.stderr)
        return backup_results
    return filtered_results

import os, sys, json, joblib
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

class PatternClassifier:

    def __init__(self, patterns_dir, decision_tree_model_path=None, padding_value=1514):
        """
        Initialize classifier

        Parameters:
        patterns_dir: Directory containing range pattern JSON files
        decision_tree_model_path: Path to decision tree model file
        padding_value: Padding value used for early termination mechanism
        """
        self.patterns_dir = patterns_dir
        self.padding_value = padding_value
        self.patterns = {}
        self.sorted_patterns = []
        self.class_names = []
        self.decision_tree_model = None
        self.decision_tree_model_path = decision_tree_model_path
        self.load_patterns()
        self.load_decision_tree()

    def load_patterns(self):
        """
        Load all range patterns from directory
        """
        patterns_path = Path(self.patterns_dir)
        if not patterns_path.exists():
            raise ValueError(f'Pattern directory {self.patterns_dir} does not exist!')
        json_files = list(patterns_path.glob('*.json'))
        if not json_files:
            raise ValueError(f'No JSON files found in directory {self.patterns_dir}!')
        print(f'Loading {len(json_files)} pattern files...', file=sys.stderr)
        all_patterns = []
        for json_file in json_files:
            class_name = json_file.stem
            try:
                with open(json_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                    patterns_data = json.load(f)
                if class_name not in self.patterns:
                    self.patterns[class_name] = []
                for pattern_item in patterns_data:
                    if isinstance(pattern_item, list) and len(pattern_item) == 2:
                        (pattern, priority) = pattern_item
                        self.patterns[class_name].append((pattern, priority))
                        all_patterns.append((pattern, priority, class_name))
                    else:
                        print(f'  Warning: Skipping pattern with incorrect format: {pattern_item}', file=sys.stderr)
                self.patterns[class_name].sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
                print(f"  Loaded class '{class_name}': {len(self.patterns[class_name])} patterns", file=sys.stderr)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f'  Warning: Error loading file {json_file}: {str(e)}', file=sys.stderr)
        self.sorted_patterns = sorted(all_patterns, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        self.class_names = sorted(self.patterns.keys())
        total_patterns = len(self.sorted_patterns)
        print(f'\nTotal loaded {len(self.class_names)} classes, {total_patterns} patterns', file=sys.stderr)
        print(f'Classes: {self.class_names}', file=sys.stderr)
        if total_patterns > 0:
            print(f'Priority range: {self.sorted_patterns[0][1]} (highest) -> {self.sorted_patterns[-1][1]} (lowest)', file=sys.stderr)

    def load_decision_tree(self):
        """
        Load decision tree model
        """
        if self.decision_tree_model_path and os.path.exists(self.decision_tree_model_path):
            try:
                self.decision_tree_model = joblib.load(self.decision_tree_model_path)
                print(f'Loaded decision tree model: {self.decision_tree_model_path}', file=sys.stderr)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f'Warning: Failed to load decision tree model: {str(e)}', file=sys.stderr)
                self.decision_tree_model = None
        elif self.decision_tree_model_path:
            print(f'Warning: Decision tree model file does not exist: {self.decision_tree_model_path}', file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            print('Decision tree model path not provided, will only use pattern matching', file=sys.stderr)

    def check_pattern_match(self, sample, pattern):
        """
        Check if sample can match pattern at some position, with early termination mechanism

        Parameters:
        sample: Sample sequence (1D array)
        pattern: Pattern range list [[x0,y0], [x1,y1], ...]

        Returns:
        tuple: (match_end_position, sample_length)
               match_end_position: start_pos + pattern_length if matched, -1 if not matched
        """
        sample_length = 30
        for i in range(len(sample)):
            if sample[i] == self.padding_value:
                sample_length = i + 1
                break
        pattern_length = len(pattern)
        if pattern_length > sample_length:
            return (-1, sample_length)
        for start_pos in range(sample_length - pattern_length + 1):
            if sample[start_pos] == self.padding_value:
                break
            match = True
            for (i, (x_min, x_max)) in enumerate(pattern):
                sample_value = sample[start_pos + i]
                if sample_value == self.padding_value:
                    match = False
                    break
                if not x_min <= sample_value <= x_max:
                    match = False
                    break
            if match:
                return (start_pos + pattern_length, sample_length)
        return (-1, sample_length)

    def predict_sample(self, sample):
        """
        Predict class for single sample, first try pattern matching, use decision tree if failed

        Parameters:
        sample: Sample sequence (1D array)

        Returns:
        tuple: (predicted_class, confidence_score, match_pos, method)
               method: 'pattern' or 'decision_tree'
        """
        for (pattern, priority, class_name) in self.sorted_patterns:
            (match_pos, sample_length) = self.check_pattern_match(sample, pattern)
            if match_pos != -1:
                return (class_name, 1.0, match_pos, 'pattern')
        if self.decision_tree_model is not None:
            try:
                sample_flattened = sample.reshape(1, -1)
                tree_pred = self.decision_tree_model.predict(sample_flattened[:, :4])[0]
                confidence = 1.0
                if hasattr(self.decision_tree_model, 'predict_proba'):
                    proba = self.decision_tree_model.predict_proba(sample_flattened[:, :4])[0]
                    confidence = np.max(proba)
                if isinstance(tree_pred, (int, np.integer)):
                    if tree_pred < len(self.class_names):
                        predicted_class = self.class_names[tree_pred]
                    else:
                        predicted_class = f'class_{tree_pred}'
                else:
                    predicted_class = str(tree_pred)
                match_pos = sample_length
                return (predicted_class, confidence, match_pos, 'decision_tree')
            except Exception as e:
                print(f'Decision tree prediction error: {str(e)}', file=sys.stderr)
        return (None, 0.0, -1, 'none')

    def predict_batch(self, samples):
        """
        Predict class for batch of samples

        Parameters:
        samples: List of samples

        Returns:
        list: [(predicted_class, confidence, match_pos, method), ...]
        """
        predictions = []
        for sample in samples:
            (pred_class, confidence, match_pos, method) = self.predict_sample(sample)
            predictions.append((pred_class, confidence, match_pos, method))
        return predictions

"""Trusted child bootstrap, loaded by the public runner before any submission."""
import ctypes
import errno
import os
import resource
import signal
import sys
import types


class Filter(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [('code', ctypes.c_ushort), ('jt', ctypes.c_ubyte),
                ('jf', ctypes.c_ubyte), ('k', ctypes.c_uint)]


class Program(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [('length', ctypes.c_ushort), ('filters', ctypes.POINTER(Filter))]


def restrict():
    # Published v3 candidate numeric limits; inherited syscall deny policy.
    for kind, values in [(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (1024*1024**2,)*2),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_CPU, (120, 121)),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (32, 32)),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_NPROC, (64, 64)),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (64*1024**2,)*2),
                         (resource.RLIMIT_CORE, (0, 0))]:
        resource.setrlimit(kind, values)
    if os.uname().machine != 'x86_64':
        raise OSError('public worker requires Linux x86_64')
    denied = [29, 30, 31, 41, 42, 53, 56, 57, 58, 62, 64, 65, 66,
              68, 69, 70, 71, 101, 105, 106, 109, 112, 113, 114,
              116, 117, 119, 155, 161, 165, 166, 200, 220, 234,
              248, 249, 250, 272, 298, 303, 304, 308, 310, 311,
              321, 323, 425, 426, 427, 438]
    # Linux x86_64 BPF ABI: architecture guard, x32 guard, clone3=ENOSYS,
    # then EPERM for every denied call, including all process/thread creation.
    instructions = [(0x20, 0, 0, 4), (0x15, 1, 0, 0xc000003e),
                    (0x06, 0, 0, 0x80000000), (0x20, 0, 0, 0),
                    (0x35, 0, 1, 0x40000000), (0x06, 0, 0, 0x80000000),
                    (0x15, 0, 1, 435), (0x06, 0, 0, 0x50000 | errno.ENOSYS)]
    for nr in denied:
        instructions.extend([(0x15, 0, 1, nr), (0x06, 0, 0, 0x50000 | errno.EPERM)])
    instructions.append((0x06, 0, 0, 0x7fff0000))
    array = (Filter * len(instructions))(*(Filter(*row) for row in instructions))
    program = Program(len(instructions), array)
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
    if libc.prctl(4, 0, 0, 0, 0) or libc.prctl(38, 1, 0, 0, 0) or libc.prctl(22, 2, ctypes.byref(program), 0, 0):
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), 'public child seccomp setup failed')


def main():
    if os.geteuid() == 0:
        raise OSError('public child refuses root')
    source_fd, filename, scratch = int(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
    source = bytearray()
    while True:
        block = os.read(source_fd, 65536)
        if not block:
            break
        source.extend(block)
        if len(source) > 64*1024**2:
            raise OSError('submission byte budget exceeded')
    os.close(source_fd)
    os.chdir(scratch)
    # The parent blocks termination during spawn; restore normal child signals.
    signal.pthread_sigmask(signal.SIG_SETMASK, [])
    restrict()  # Fail closed: submitted code is never executed on setup failure.
    sys.path.insert(0,os.path.dirname(filename))
    sys.path.insert(0,os.environ['SYNECDOCHE_SITE'])
    module = types.ModuleType('__main__')
    module.__file__ = filename
    module.__package__ = None
    module.__spec__ = None
    sys.modules['__main__'] = module
    sys.argv = [filename]
    exec(compile(bytes(source), filename, 'exec'), module.__dict__)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

    total = sum(scores[begin:begin + width])

"""CPU backup-tree training path.

The backup classifier is the pinned scikit-learn decision tree; the tree node
order of the fitted model is the certificate order.
"""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier

PADDING = 1514


def training_matrix(rows, width):
    """First ``width`` encoded values of every row, right-padded with 1514."""
    data = np.full((len(rows), width), PADDING, dtype=np.int64)
    for index, row in enumerate(rows):
        values = row['values'][:width]
        if values:
            data[index, :len(values)] = values
    return data


def train_backup(features, labels):
    """Fit the pinned backup decision tree."""
    model = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=10, random_state=42, class_weight='balanced')
    model.fit(features, labels)
    return model


def tree_certificate(model):
    """Native tree-node order certificate of a fitted backup tree."""
    tree = model.tree_
    nodes = []
    for index in range(int(tree.node_count)):
        left = int(tree.children_left[index])
        if left < 0:
            values = tree.value[index][0]
            best = values.max()
            choice = min(position for position, value in enumerate(values) if value == best)
            nodes.append([int(model.classes_[choice])])
        else:
            nodes.append([int(tree.feature[index]),
                          int(round(2 * float(tree.threshold[index]))),
                          left,
                          int(tree.children_right[index])])
    return nodes


def predict(nodes, features, width):
    """Class predicted by the backup tree for one epoch prefix."""
    sample = list(features[:width])
    while len(sample) < width:
        sample.append(PADDING)
    node = 0
    while True:
        entry = nodes[node]
        if len(entry) == 1:
            return entry[0]
        feature, doubled, left, right = entry
        node = left if 2 * sample[feature] <= doubled else right

"""Online pattern matching structures of one release bank.

A range bank keeps one generalized interval per kept cluster, an exact bank
keeps one table per pattern length.  Both are matched against the contiguous
suffix of the epoch that ends at the arriving packet.
"""
from collections import defaultdict

PADDING = 1514
VALUE_MAX = 3028


def build_tables(patterns):
    """Per coordinate tables mapping a value to the clusters that accept it.

    ``patterns`` is the list of interval vectors of one pattern length; the
    tables are indexed by the cluster position inside that list.
    """
    length = len(patterns[0])
    tables = []
    for position in range(length):
        events = []
        for index, bounds in enumerate(patterns):
            bit = 1 << index
            events.append((bounds[position][0], bit))
            events.append((bounds[position][1] + 1, bit))
        events.sort()
        table = [0] * (VALUE_MAX + 1)
        mask = 0
        cursor = 0
        for value in range(VALUE_MAX + 1):
            while cursor < len(events) and events[cursor][0] == value:
                mask ^= events[cursor][1]
                cursor += 1
            table[value] = mask
        tables.append(table)
    return tables


class PatternBank:
    """Kept clusters of one release, ordered by deployment priority."""

    def __init__(self, clusters):
        # clusters: kept clusters in priority order
        self.clusters = clusters
        self.groups = {}
        grouped = defaultdict(list)
        for rank, cluster in enumerate(clusters):
            grouped[len(cluster['bounds'])].append((rank, cluster))
        for length, items in grouped.items():
            patterns = [cluster['bounds'] for _, cluster in items]
            self.groups[length] = {
                'clusters': [cluster for _, cluster in items],
                'ranks': [rank for rank, _ in items],
                'tables': build_tables(patterns),
            }

    def match(self, features):
        """Highest priority cluster matching the suffix that ends here."""
        count = len(features)
        best_rank = None
        best = None
        for length, group in self.groups.items():
            if length > count:
                continue
            base = count - length
            mask = None
            tables = group['tables']
            for position in range(length):
                allowed = tables[position][features[base + position]]
                if not allowed:
                    mask = None
                    break
                mask = allowed if mask is None else (mask & allowed)
            if mask:
                index = (mask & -mask).bit_length() - 1
                rank = group['ranks'][index]
                if best_rank is None or rank < best_rank:
                    best_rank = rank
                    best = group['clusters'][index]
        return best

            else:

            raise ValueError('invalid_request')

        else:

"""Local stand-in for the public runner (setsid is denied in this sandbox)."""
import json, os, pathlib, subprocess, sys, time

BASE = pathlib.Path('/workspace')
SUB = BASE / 'submission'
SITE = BASE / 'site'


def invoke(data: bytes, timeout=180):
    env = {'PATH': '/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin', 'HOME': '/tmp', 'LANG': 'C', 'LC_ALL': 'C',
           'TMPDIR': '/tmp', 'PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE': '1', 'PYTHONUNBUFFERED': '1',
           'PYTHONHASHSEED': '0', 'OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS': '1', 'OMP_NUM_THREADS': '1',
           'MKL_NUM_THREADS': '1', 'SYNECDOCHE_SITE': str(SITE),
           'LD_LIBRARY_PATH': str(BASE / 'native')}
    start = time.monotonic()
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-I', '-B', str(SUB / 'run.py')], input=data,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env, timeout=timeout)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr, time.monotonic() - start


def main():
    fixtures = json.loads((BASE / 'examples.json').read_text())
    ok = True
    for case in fixtures:
        data = (case['raw'].encode() if 'raw' in case else
                json.dumps(case['request'], separators=(',', ':')).encode())
        rc, out, err, secs = invoke(data)
        if rc:
            print('FAIL', case['name'], 'rc', rc, err.decode()[:2000])
            ok = False
            continue
        try:
            answer = json.loads(out.decode('utf-8'))
        except Exception as exc:
            print('FAIL', case['name'], 'bad json', exc, out[:400])
            ok = False
            continue
        if json.dumps(answer, sort_keys=True) != json.dumps(case['response'], sort_keys=True):
            print('FAIL', case['name'], 'mismatch')
            print(' got', json.dumps(answer, sort_keys=True)[:3000])
            print(' exp', json.dumps(case['response'], sort_keys=True)[:3000])
            ok = False
        else:
            print('PASS', case['name'], '%.2fs' % secs)
    print('OK' if ok else 'FAILURES')
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

"""Cross-check the optimized pipeline against the slow reference."""
import json, random, sys, os
from fractions import Fraction

sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/submission')
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/dev')
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/site')

import reference as ref
from release import Release


def rnd_values(rng, length, pad=False):
    values = [rng.choice([1514, rng.randrange(0, 3029)]) for _ in range(length)]
    # keep the encoding meaningful: most values are near 1514
    values = [rng.randrange(1200, 1800) if rng.random() < 0.8 else rng.randrange(0, 3029)
              for _ in range(length)]
    if pad and length > 2:
        cut = rng.randrange(1, length)
        values = values[:cut] + [1514] * (length - cut)
    return values


def make_release(rng, rid):
    classes = rng.randrange(1, 4)
    width = rng.randrange(2, 5)
    ndisc = rng.randrange(0, 7)
    discovery = []
    for _ in range(ndisc):
        length = rng.randrange(2, 14)
        values = rnd_values(rng, length, pad=rng.random() < 0.3)
        activation = [rng.randrange(0, 20) for _ in values]
        discovery.append({'class': rng.randrange(classes), 'values': values,
                          'activation': activation})
    train = [{'class': c, 'values': rnd_values(rng, rng.randrange(0, 6), pad=False)} for c in range(classes)]
    validation = [{'class': c, 'values': rnd_values(rng, rng.randrange(0, 6), pad=False)} for c in range(classes)]
    eps = Fraction(rng.randrange(1, 60), rng.randrange(1, 60))
    ratio = Fraction(rng.randrange(0, 5), rng.randrange(1, 6))
    threshold = Fraction(rng.randrange(0, 3), rng.randrange(1, 4))
    return {'id': rid, 'classes': classes, 'width': width,
            'eps': [eps.numerator, eps.denominator],
            'ratio': [ratio.numerator, ratio.denominator],
            'threshold': [threshold.numerator, threshold.denominator],
            'mode': rng.choice(['range', 'exact']),
            'packet_limit': rng.randrange(width, 12), 'idle_us': rng.choice([0, 1, 5, 100]),
            'discovery': discovery, 'train': train, 'validation': validation}


def compare(rng, trials=200):
    for trial in range(trials):
        release = make_release(rng, 'r%d' % trial)
        capacity = {'range': rng.randrange(0, 20), 'exact': rng.randrange(0, 20)}
        # reference
        frags = ref.fragments_of(release)
        clusters, noise = ref.clusters_of(frags, Fraction(*release['eps']), Fraction(*release['ratio']))
        bounds = {c['id']: ref.range_of(frags, c) for c in clusters}
        # the reference range uses floats; snap near-integers
        for cid, b in bounds.items():
            fixed = []
            for lo, hi in b:
                fixed.append([lo, hi])
            bounds[cid] = fixed
        ref.calibrate_ref(clusters, release, bounds)
        # implementation
        impl = Release(release, capacity)
        problems = []
        if [(f['row'], f['start'], f['length']) for f in impl.fragments] != \
           [(f['row'], f['start'], f['length']) for f in frags]:
            problems.append('fragments differ')
        if list(impl.noise) != list(noise):
            problems.append('noise differ %s vs %s' % (impl.noise, noise))
        if len(impl.clusters) != len(clusters):
            problems.append('cluster count %d vs %d' % (len(impl.clusters), len(clusters)))
        else:
            for a, b in zip(impl.clusters, clusters):
                if a['id'] != b['id'] or a['class'] != b['class'] or \
                   list(a['members']) != list(b['members']) or list(a['core']) != list(b['core']):
                    problems.append('cluster identity %s vs %s' % (a, b))
                    break
                if a['bounds'] != bounds[a['id']]:
                    problems.append('range %s vs %s for %s' % (a['bounds'], bounds[a['id']], a['id']))
                    break
                if list(a['hits']) != list(b['hits']):
                    problems.append('hits %s vs %s' % (a['hits'], b['hits']))
                    break
                if a['score'] != b['score']:
                    problems.append('score %s vs %s' % (a['score'], b['score']))
                    break
                if bool(a['kept']) != bool(b['kept']):
                    problems.append('kept %s vs %s' % (a['kept'], b['kept']))
                    break
        impl_entries = impl.entries
        ref_entries = ref.exact_entries_ref(clusters, bounds, capacity['exact']) if release['mode'] == 'exact' else len([c for c in clusters if c['kept']])
        if impl_entries != ref_entries:
            problems.append('entries %s vs %s' % (impl_entries, ref_entries))
        if problems:
            print('TRIAL', trial, 'PROBLEMS:', problems)
            print(json.dumps(release, indent=1)[:2000])
            return False
    return True


if __name__ == '__main__':
    rng = random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 7)
    print('OK' if compare(rng, int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 300) else 'FAILED')

"""Post-inference pipeline integration: discovery, calibration and replay."""
from release import Release
from sessions import SessionEngine


def execute(request):
    """Build the certificate of one whole request."""
    capacity = request['capacity']
    releases = [Release(spec, capacity) for spec in request['releases']]
    # The derived fragment budget spans every release of the request.
    if sum(len(release.fragments) for release in releases) > 4096:
        raise ValueError('invalid_request')
    catalog = [release.catalog() for release in releases]
    engine = SessionEngine(releases, capacity)
    installs, decisions, final = engine.execute(request['blocks'])
    return {'catalog': catalog, 'installs': installs, 'decisions': decisions, 'final': final}

import replay_ref
from release import Release
from sessions import SessionEngine


def make_release(rng, rid):
    classes = rng.randrange(1, 3)
    width = rng.randrange(2, 5)
    disc = []
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(0, 5)):
        length = rng.randrange(2, 10)
        values = [rng.randrange(1400, 1600) for _ in range(length)]
        activation = [0] * (length - 2) + [100, 100]
        disc.append({'class': rng.randrange(classes), 'values': values, 'activation': activation})
    train = [{'class': c, 'values': [rng.randrange(1400, 1600) for _ in range(width)]}
             for c in range(classes)]
    validation = [{'class': c, 'values': [rng.randrange(1400, 1600) for _ in range(rng.randrange(0, 6))]}
                  for c in range(classes)]
    return {'id': rid, 'classes': classes, 'width': width,
            'eps': [rng.randrange(1, 40), rng.randrange(1, 40)],
            'ratio': [rng.randrange(0, 3), rng.randrange(1, 3)],
            'threshold': [rng.randrange(0, 2), rng.randrange(1, 3)],
            'mode': rng.choice(['range', 'exact']),
            'packet_limit': rng.randrange(width, 8), 'idle_us': rng.choice([0, 1, 3, 50]),
            'discovery': disc, 'train': train, 'validation': validation}


def reference_catalog(release):
    item = release.catalog()
    item['mode'] = release.mode
    item['width'] = release.width
    item['idle_us'] = release.idle_us
    item['packet_limit'] = release.packet_limit
    item['kept_clusters'] = [c for c in release.clusters if c['kept']]
    item['cluster_by_id'] = {c['id']: {'id': c['id'], 'class': c['class'],
                                        'range': [list(b) for b in c['bounds']]}
                              for c in release.clusters}
    return item


def random_blocks(rng, releases, flows):
    blocks = []
    events = []
    for rid in releases:
        events.append(['install', rid])
    active = set()
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(0, 40)):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.25:
            rid = rng.choice(list(releases))
            events.append(['install', rid])
        elif choice < 0.45 and len(active) < 4:
            fid = rng.choice(flows)
            if fid not in active:
                active.add(fid)
                events.append(['open', fid])
        elif choice < 0.8 and active:
            fid = rng.choice(sorted(active))
            events.append(['packet', fid, rng.randrange(0, 20), rng.randrange(0, 2),
                           rng.randrange(1, 200)])
        elif active:
            fid = rng.choice(sorted(active))
            active.discard(fid)
            events.append(['close', fid])
    for fid in sorted(active):
        events.append(['close', fid])
    # split into blocks
    index = 0
    while index < len(events):
        size = rng.randrange(1, 5)
        blocks.append(events[index:index + size])
        index += size
    return blocks

        capacity = {'range': rng.randrange(0, 6), 'exact': rng.randrange(0, 6)}
        flows = ['f%d' % index for index in range(rng.randrange(1, 4))]

        request = {'capacity': capacity, 'releases': specs, 'blocks': blocks}

            print(json.dumps(request)[:3000])
            return False

        installs, decisions, final = got
        e_installs, e_decisions, e_final = expected
        if json.dumps(installs, sort_keys=True) != json.dumps(e_installs, sort_keys=True):
            print('TRIAL', trial, 'installs differ')
            print(' got', json.dumps(installs, sort_keys=True)[:2000])
            print(' exp', json.dumps(e_installs, sort_keys=True)[:2000])
            print(json.dumps(request)[:4000])

        validation.append({'class': 0, 'values': list(values)})

        'eps': [1, 1], 'ratio': [0, 1], 'threshold': [1, 1], 'mode': mode,
        'packet_limit': 10, 'idle_us': 1000,
        'discovery': discovery,
        'train': [{'class': 0, 'values': list(groups[0][0])}],
        'validation': validation}]}

sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/submission')
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace/site')

from release import Release

FAILURES = []


def check(name, got, expected):
    if got == expected:
        print('PASS', name)
    else:
        print('FAIL', name, 'got', got, 'expected', expected)
        FAILURES.append(name)


def brute(catalog, capacity):
    """Distinct exact keys of the kept clusters, clipped to capacity + 1."""
    tables = {}
    for cluster in catalog['clusters']:
        if not cluster['kept']:
            continue
        bounds = cluster['range']
        for key in itertools.product(*[range(low, high + 1) for low, high in bounds]):
            if 1514 in key:
                continue
            tables.setdefault(len(bounds), set()).add(key)
    total = sum(len(v) for v in tables.values())
    return min(total, capacity + 1)


def spec(rid, groups, capacity, mode='exact', classes=1):
    """groups: list of (values, count) pairs; each group is one pattern."""
    discovery = []
    validation = []
    for values, count in groups:
        padded = [1600, 1600, 1600] + list(values)
        for _ in range(count):
            discovery.append({'class': 0, 'values': list(padded),
                              'activation': [0] * 3 + [100] * len(values)})
        validation.append({'class': 0, 'values': list(padded)})
    return {'capacity': capacity, 'releases': [{
        'id': rid, 'classes': classes, 'width': 3 + max(len(v) for v, _ in groups),
        'eps': [1, 1], 'ratio': [0, 1], 'threshold': [1, 1], 'mode': mode,
        'packet_limit': 10, 'idle_us': 1000,
        'discovery': discovery,
        'train': [{'class': 0, 'values': list(groups[0][0])}],
        'validation': validation}]}


def main():
    cases = [
        ('single pattern', [([0, 4], 2)], {'range': 8, 'exact': 64}),
        ('overlapping patterns', [([0, 4], 2), ([2, 6], 2)], {'range': 8, 'exact': 64}),
        ('different lengths', [([0, 4], 2), ([0, 2, 6], 2)], {'range': 8, 'exact': 64}),
        ('padding excluded', [([1500, 1520], 2)], {'range': 8, 'exact': 64}),
        ('clipped', [([0, 40], 2)], {'range': 8, 'exact': 10}),
        ('identical patterns', [([0, 4], 2), ([0, 4], 2)], {'range': 8, 'exact': 64}),
    ]
    for name, groups, capacity in cases:
        request = spec('a', groups, capacity)
        release = Release(request['releases'][0], request['capacity'])
        catalog = release.catalog()
        expected = brute(catalog, capacity['exact'])
        check(name, release.entries, expected)
    # a range bank has one entry per kept cluster
    request = spec('a', [([0, 4], 2), ([10, 14], 2)], {'range': 8, 'exact': 64}, mode='range')
    release = Release(request['releases'][0], request['capacity'])
    check('range bank entries', release.entries, 2)
    print('FAILURES:', FAILURES)
    return 1 if FAILURES else 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

"""Packet-segment extraction, exact pattern distance and cluster formation.

All arithmetic in this module is exact: activation thresholds, pattern
distances and cluster boundaries are decided with integer arithmetic so that
equality cases never depend on floating point rounding.
"""
from collections import defaultdict
from math import isqrt

import numpy as np
from scipy.sparse import csr_matrix
from scipy.sparse.csgraph import connected_components

PADDING = 1514
VALUE_MIN = 0
VALUE_MAX = 3028
# Saturated comparison limit for squared pattern distances.
DISTANCE_CAP = 4 * 1000 * 1000 * 1000


def real_prefix(values):
    """Encoded values before the first padding marker."""
    for index, value in enumerate(values):
        if value == PADDING:
            return values[:index]
    return values


def _best_window(scores, begin, end, width):
    """Widest-sum window of ``width`` activations inside ``[begin, end)``.

    Ties keep the earliest start, the final legal window included.
    """
    total = sum(scores[begin:begin + width])
    best = total
    best_start = begin
    for start in range(begin + 1, end - width + 1):
        total += scores[start + width - 1] - scores[start - 1]
        if total > best:
            best = total
            best_start = start
    return best_start


def extract_fragments(discovery, width):
    """Fragment certificate triples in discovery order.

    Returns a list of dictionaries with the source row, the start position,
    the fragment length, the owning class and the real feature sequence.
    """
    fragments = []
    for row_index, row in enumerate(discovery):
        values = row['values']
        activation = row['activation']
        prefix = real_prefix(values)
        count = len(prefix)
        if count < 2:
            continue
        scores = activation[:count]
        total = sum(scores)
        squares = sum(score * score for score in scores)
        # Population variance of the real prefix: spread / count**2.
        spread = count * squares - total * total
        high = []
        for score in scores:
            offset = count * score - total
            # score > mean + sigma  <=>  offset > 0 and offset**2 > spread
            high.append(offset > 0 and offset * offset > spread)
        index = 0
        while index < count:
            if not high[index]:
                index += 1
                continue
            end = index
            while end < count and high[end]:
                end += 1
            length = end - index
            if length >= 2:
                if length <= width:
                    start = index
                    span = length
                else:
                    # A longer run contributes its width long window.
                    start = _best_window(scores, index, end, width)
                    span = width
                fragments.append({'row': row_index, 'start': start, 'length': span,
                                 'class': row['class'],
                                 'sequence': tuple(values[start:start + span])})
            index = end
    return fragments


def distance_limits(length, eps):
    """Largest squared distance that still counts as a neighbour.

    ``distance <= eps`` is decided as
    ``S * 9**A * q**2 <= L * 25**A * p**2`` with ``S`` the squared coordinate
    distance sum, ``A`` the number of equal coordinates and ``eps = p/q``.
    """
    numerator = eps.numerator
    denominator = eps.denominator
    limits = []
    for equal in range(length + 1):
        bound = (length * (25 ** equal) * numerator * numerator) // ((9 ** equal) * denominator * denominator)
        limits.append(min(bound, DISTANCE_CAP))
    return limits


def neighbour_matrix(sequences, eps):
    """Boolean neighbour matrix over the fragments of one class and length."""
    count = len(sequences)
    length = len(sequences[0])
    data = np.array(sequences, dtype=np.int64)
    limits = np.array(distance_limits(length, eps), dtype=np.int64)
    below = data < PADDING
    above = data > PADDING
    matrix = np.zeros((count, count), dtype=bool)
    for index in range(count):
        diff = data[index][None, :] - data
        distance = np.abs(diff)
        crossed = (below[index][None, :] & above) | (above[index][None, :] & below)
        distance = distance + 1000 * crossed
        squared = (distance * distance).sum(axis=1)
        equal = (diff == 0).sum(axis=1)
        matrix[index] = squared <= limits[equal]
    return matrix


def cluster_fragments(fragments, eps, ratio):
    """Cluster the fragments of one release.

    Returns ``(clusters, noise)`` where every cluster carries its identifier,
    class, members, core members and the fragment indices of its members.
    """
    total = len(fragments)
    by_class = defaultdict(list)
    for index, fragment in enumerate(fragments):
        by_class[fragment['class']].append(index)
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    density = {}
    for label, indices in by_class.items():
        count = len(indices)
        # The density minimum is max(2, ceil(m * ratio)) over the whole class.
        density[label] = max(2, -(-count * ratio.numerator // ratio.denominator))
        for index in indices:
            groups[(label, len(fragments[index]['sequence']))].append(index)
    clusters = []
    claimed = set()
    for (label, length), indices in sorted(groups.items()):
        sequences = [fragments[index]['sequence'] for index in indices]
        matrix = neighbour_matrix(sequences, eps)
        degrees = matrix.sum(axis=1)
        core = degrees >= density[label]
        core_index = np.flatnonzero(core)
        if core_index.size == 0:
            continue
        _, labels = connected_components(csr_matrix(matrix[np.ix_(core_index, core_index)]),
                                         directed=False)
        component_count = int(labels.max()) + 1
        members_by_component = defaultdict(list)
        for position, node in enumerate(core_index):
            members_by_component[int(labels[position])].append(int(node))
        # The cluster identifier is the smallest core fragment identifier.
        component_min = np.zeros(component_count, dtype=np.int64)
        for number in range(component_count):
            component_min[number] = min(indices[node] for node in members_by_component[number])
        owner = {int(component_min[number]): number for number in range(component_count)}
        noncore_index = np.flatnonzero(~core)
        if noncore_index.size:
            attached = matrix[np.ix_(noncore_index, core_index)]
            choices = np.where(attached, component_min[labels][None, :], total + 1)
            best = choices.min(axis=1)
            for position, node in enumerate(noncore_index):
                target = int(best[position])
                if target <= total:
                    members_by_component[owner[target]].append(int(node))
        for number in range(component_count):
            members = sorted(indices[node] for node in members_by_component[number])
            core_members = sorted(indices[int(node)] for node in core_index[labels == number])
            claimed.update(members)
            clusters.append({'id': int(component_min[number]), 'class': label,
                             'members': members, 'core': core_members,
                             'fragments': members,
                             'length': length})
    clusters.sort(key=lambda cluster: cluster['id'])
    noise = sorted(set(range(total)) - claimed)
    return clusters, noise


def cluster_range(fragments, members):
    """Generalized interval of a cluster over all of its members."""
    sequences = [fragments[index]['sequence'] for index in members]
    count = len(sequences)
    data = np.array(sequences, dtype=np.int64)
    low = data.min(axis=0)
    high = data.max(axis=0)
    total = data.sum(axis=0)
    squares = (data * data).sum(axis=0)
    spread = count * squares - total * total
    bounds = []
    for position in range(data.shape[1]):
        deviation = int(spread[position])
        root = isqrt(deviation)
        exact = root * root == deviation
        upper = (int(high[position]) * count + root) // count
        scaled = int(low[position]) * count
        if scaled * scaled >= deviation:
            # low - sigma is not negative, truncation towards zero is the floor
            shifted = scaled - root
            lower = shifted // count
            if not exact and shifted % count == 0:
                lower -= 1
        else:
            lower = 0
        bounds.append([max(VALUE_MIN, lower), min(VALUE_MAX, upper)])
    return bounds

"""One release: discovery certificate, calibration, backup tree and bank."""
from fractions import Fraction

import numpy as np

from offline_discovery.rule_generate import cluster_fragments, cluster_range, extract_fragments
from offline_discovery.rule_remove import calibrate, exact_entry_count
from online_matching.match_p4 import PatternBank
from online_matching.train_rf import train_backup, training_matrix, tree_certificate


class Release:
    """Deployment model of one release identifier."""

    def __init__(self, spec, capacity):
        self.id = spec['id']
        self.classes = spec['classes']
        self.width = spec['width']
        self.eps = Fraction(spec['eps'][0], spec['eps'][1])
        self.ratio = Fraction(spec['ratio'][0], spec['ratio'][1])
        self.threshold = Fraction(spec['threshold'][0], spec['threshold'][1])
        self.mode = spec['mode']
        self.packet_limit = spec['packet_limit']
        self.idle_us = spec['idle_us']
        # Discovery fragments and their clustering.
        self.fragments = extract_fragments(spec['discovery'], self.width)
        clusters, noise = cluster_fragments(self.fragments, self.eps, self.ratio)
        for cluster in clusters:
            cluster['bounds'] = cluster_range(self.fragments, cluster['fragments'])
        calibrate(clusters, spec['validation'], self.classes, self.threshold)
        self.clusters = clusters
        self.noise = noise
        # Deployment priority: decreasing exact score, then increasing cluster id.
        self.kept = sorted((cluster for cluster in clusters if cluster['kept']),
                           key=lambda cluster: (-cluster['score'], cluster['id']))
        self.priority = [cluster['id'] for cluster in self.kept]
        self.bank = PatternBank(self.kept)
        # Backup classifier of the release.
        rows = spec['train']
        features = training_matrix(rows, self.width)
        labels = np.array([row['class'] for row in rows], dtype=np.int64)
        self.model = train_backup(features, labels)
        self.nodes = tree_certificate(self.model)
        # Bank size: one entry per kept cluster, or the clipped exact table size.
        if self.mode == 'range':
            self.entries = len(self.kept)
        else:
            self.entries = exact_entry_count(self.kept, capacity['exact'])

    def catalog(self):
        """Catalog item of this release."""
        clusters = []
        for cluster in self.clusters:
            score = cluster['score']
            clusters.append({'id': cluster['id'], 'class': cluster['class'],
                             'members': list(cluster['members']), 'core': list(cluster['core']),
                             'range': [list(bound) for bound in cluster['bounds']],
                             'hits': list(cluster['hits']),
                             'score': [score.numerator, score.denominator],
                             'kept': bool(cluster['kept'])})
        return {'id': self.id,
                'fragments': [[fragment['row'], fragment['start'], fragment['length']]
                              for fragment in self.fragments],
                'noise': list(self.noise),
                'clusters': clusters,
                'priority': list(self.priority),
                'backup': [list(node) for node in self.nodes],
                'entries': self.entries}
